title: Unbounded right derivation of an additive tower functor commutes with evaluation
statement:
Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian], let $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be additive [def-weil-pbc-additive-functor], and let $\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A)=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{op},\mathcal A)$, with the analogous notation for $\mathcal B$ [def-weil-inverse-system]. Use ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Assume every cochain complex in $\mathcal A$ and in $\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A)$ admits a quasi-isomorphism to a K-injective complex; K-injective means that every chain map from an acyclic complex is null-homotopic. Let $F^{\operatorname{Tow}}$ apply $F$ to all tower objects and transitions. Both total right derived functors $RF:D(\mathcal A)\to D(\mathcal B)$ and $R(F^{\operatorname{Tow}}):D(\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A))\to D(\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal B))$ exist with universal units $\eta_F,\eta_{F^{\operatorname{Tow}}}$ [def-sfb-right-derived-functor]. If $e_n$ denotes exact evaluation and its termwise derived functor, there are specified natural isomorphisms
$$\beta_n:e_nR(F^{\operatorname{Tow}})\xrightarrow{\sim}(RF)e_n.$$
For every tower complex $P$, with the canonical localization/evaluation identifications, they satisfy
$$\beta_{n,QP}\circ e_n(\eta_{F^{\operatorname{Tow}},P})=\eta_{F,P_n}.$$
For any K-injective tower resolution $P\to I$, the evaluated map $P_n\to I_n$ is a quasi-isomorphism, $I_n$ is K-injective, and $\beta_{n,QP}$ is the identification of both sides with $Q(F(I_n))$ induced by that same resolution and the derived units. These identifications are independent of resolution and natural for every morphism in $D(\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A))$. For every $m\geq n$, write $t^{\mathcal A}_{m,n}:e_m\to e_n$ and $t^{\mathcal B}_{m,n}:e_m\to e_n$ for the transformations induced by the actual tower arrows, localized degreewise [def-coef-tower-derived-evaluation-transition]. Then
$$\beta_n\circ(t^{\mathcal B}_{m,n}R(F^{\operatorname{Tow}}))=((RF)t^{\mathcal A}_{m,n})\circ\beta_m.$$
This includes identity and composite transitions. No exactness of $F$, left-adjoint hypothesis on $F$, boundedness, or exactness of infinite products is assumed.

proof.text: Use the universal pairs and invertibility on K-injectives from [def-sfb-right-derived-functor] (constructed by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived]). By [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian] evaluation is exact additive. Its canonical factor is [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. Transport the homotopy units to cochain units along the quotient/Qh comparisons. Since termwise F commutes strictly with evaluation, the evaluated tower unit a and the evaluated-input unit b are natural transformations with a common source.

On a K-injective tower I both a and b are invertible: for b, apply [lem-weil-tower-evaluation-kinjective] before using unit invertibility from [def-sfb-right-derived-functor]. Define d_I = a_I inverse followed by b_I. Naturality of a and b proves naturality of d on complex maps. By [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], every derived map between QI and QJ is represented by a homotopy class, and the homotopy quotient is full, so this proves naturality for every such derived map.

Choose a representative complex for each derived object X and apply the given resolution hypothesis to obtain e_X : X ≅ QI_X. Define beta_X = R(a tower)(e_X), followed by d_I_X, followed by RF(evaluated e_X inverse). Naturality on maps between K-injective representatives proves naturality of beta and its agreement with d_I on every QI. The components are invertible, giving a natural isomorphism on the entire derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Naturality along any resolution K → I and cancellation of the isomorphism on its target gives a_K beta_QK = b_K for every complex K. Postcompose with RF of the evaluation factor to obtain exactly the stated cochain-unit equation.

For every resolution f:P → I, evaluation preserves the quasi-isomorphism by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] and preserves K-injectivity by [lem-weil-tower-evaluation-kinjective]. Directly unfold the canonical comparison c_f of [def-sfb-right-derived-functor] and cancel its inverse unit to obtain c_f eta_I = RF(Qf). Postcompose the desired resolution equation with the invertible unit at I_n. Naturality of the evaluation factor and beta, the unit equation at I, and the same identity for the tower comparison identify the two sides. This works for every resolution and the same beta; its natural-isomorphism type already supplies naturality for all derived morphisms.

The definition [def-coef-tower-derived-evaluation-transition] and Localization.liftNatTrans_app identify each transition on QI, conjugated by the evaluation factors, with Q of the actual transition of complexes. Naturality of the tower unit and the base unit gives a_m t_B = Q(F(I(t))) a_n and b_m RF(t_A) = Q(F(I(t))) b_n. Substitute a beta = b and cancel a_m on K-injective I. The two sides are natural transformations on the derived category; naturality along a resolution of any complex, then localization extensionality, gives equality on every object. Identity and composite arrows are included because t is arbitrary. No product exactness or adjunction for F is needed.
